intent: Hold the iteration 1 reference geometry unchanged for the final iteration. Kept: five 12 mm sensors at y = 0.05 m spanning ±0.03 m, with the wheel, body and mass values as they are. Changed: nothing. Expected result: a score near 69.3 if the Integrator's controller matches the reference, with line_loss_events about 1 per run. Under consideration without commitment: a single wheel_track or mass test, but only if line loss clearly falls in the race, and that is not possible within this iteration.
learning: Ten races have now mapped the sensor layout: span ±0.03 m at 12 mm and y = 0.05 m is the best measured. Controller changes moved the score by up to about 13 points on this geometry, so the controller, not the layout, governs further gains. Untested levers remain wheel_track and mass.
rationale: The evidence across iterations 0 to 10 points to one layout. Five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 m and y = 0.05 m scored 69.3241 in iterations 1, 4 and 6 with the same controller, so the result is reproducible. Every single geometry change tested lowered the score with the controller held fixed: the 16 mm footprint (54.45, iteration 2), y = 0.03 m (59.64, iteration 3) and the span of ±0.04 m (52.47, iteration 5). Line loss has stayed at about 1 per run (1.0 to 1.65) under every geometry, and steering oscillation (0.07 to 0.15) is not limiting. Later score swings (61.77, 56.44, 63.59) came from controller changes on this same geometry, so the controller is the lever now. The Integrator's advice is to hold the geometry. I took it, because this is the final iteration and the final unseen-track race will be scored on whatever design is delivered here. An untested dynamics change (wheel_track or mass) would be a gamble with no line-loss evidence behind it, and the feedback says to test one only if line loss clearly falls, which it has not. Body width does not move the off-track limit (max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) = 0.06 m across the range), so it is not a lever. Expected result: about 69.3 if the controller matches the reference, with line loss near 1 per run.
